title: I Used the Company Mileage Spreadsheet on the Director's Weekend Trip

parts.text: I processed expenses at 3:10 p.m. and Director Patel's mileage started at our office and ended at a lake house on Saturday. The spreadsheet he required from us said business dates only, no weekends without pre-approval. I was thirty, AP specialist, holding a pivot table. He had denied my Tuesday client mileage because I stopped for gas off-route. I highlighted Saturday, the lake, and his own instruction tab. Then I routed it back as incomplete instead of approved. At 3:22 he pinged that lakes can be offsites.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He wants an offsite code for a Saturday lake with no pre-approval.

social.video_title: His mileage ended at a lake house on Saturday — Part 1/2
social.description: AP pivot, denied gas stop, instruction tab. Lakes as offsites. Would you have approved it to be nice?

parts.text: Finance asked for the offsite agenda. There was a photo of a dock. The line came out of the report. My Tuesday mileage posted with a note that gas is a business liquid. Patel filed weekdays. The spreadsheet did not grow a lake column. I still stop for gas. I still highlight. Incomplete is a kindness that keeps docks off the ledger.

social.video_title: The dock photo was not an agenda — Part 2/2
social.description: Line removed, Tuesday posted, no lake column. Was a weekend a client?
